# Offline original MSI qualification

The **Windows Offline Original MSI Proof** workflow uses a disposable Windows 2022 runner and a successful original installer build. The draft pull request pins the 1.9.0 installer from workflow run `44902072714`, manufacturing job `136839869378`, and source `272ee64e929bdfd2ebbf5e1f912221862ec5f9d2`. To qualify a different SHA, update `candidate.json` on a new proof topic and open a separate QA draft. When manual dispatch is available, provide the original Windows build run ID, full source SHA, expected app version, and expected database revision. The original run must have its installer artifacts available.

Setup downloads and hashes each original artifact ZIP, matches MSI and all CAB bytes and Media entries to verified build provenance, and stages the pinned Playwright dependency lock before measurement. A preview execution of the independently scheduled SYSTEM recovery task must succeed before the harness changes Windows Firewall. The watchdog restores the original policy and hosts file if the controller stops. Setup, installation, and network controls are guarded for the dedicated GitHub-hosted workflow.

The proof enables deny-by-default Windows Firewall on all profiles. The only external exception is TCP port 443 for the exact authenticated Actions listener and worker executables, with their control-plane hostnames pinned locally during measurement. It resolves `api.github.com` once online and checks direct TCP connectivity to the same addresses before, throughout, and after isolation. Independent controls run under SYSTEM and the actual ordinary account. Effective firewall rules and the runner TLS connection are checked at each product phase.

The test uses the original MSI with `/i`, verifies product registration, and launches the installed shell and packaged loopback sidecar as a fresh Windows user at medium integrity. The tracked first-use WebView2 journey imports and reviews source pixels, reopens them in the editor, and downloads YOLO. A second installed desktop and sidecar reopen the same managed profile and verify the exact saved image hash and annotation. The scratch cache moves only after the owned browser processes exit and Windows releases its file handles. The wait is bounded and leaves other browser processes alone. The Windows Firewall event journal must record its own setup control and report no policy change during product operations. Each TCP sampling gap must stay within 10 seconds. Recovery, temporary account removal, and uninstall finish before evidence upload.

The `cached-upgrade` runner also stages the exact validated 1.8.0 MSI and six cabinets. Before isolation its ordinary user creates a reviewed project and a verified recovery backup with the registered predecessor. Under outbound deny, the original 1.9.0 MSI replaces the 1.8.0 registration. The same ordinary principal opens and restarts the new desktop, with the original image bytes and saved annotation verified through its own loopback backend. The upgraded installation restores the verified pre-upgrade backup into a new folder. The separately extracted exact 1.8.0 shell, launched by the same ordinary user under ongoing denial, reopens that recovery at its old schema.

The workflow uploads `ReefVision-Windows-Offline-MSI-Proof-fresh` and `ReefVision-Windows-Offline-MSI-Proof-cached-upgrade` separately. Their reports bind the original MSI, installed binary hashes, source and test identities, control phases, launch IDs and persisted review. Their TCP control JSONL files, `watchdog.jsonl`, transport and payload receipts, MSI logs, and native journey receipts document the observed inputs and outcomes. Both runners already include WebView2 and Windows components.
